key_insight: ISLA builds physical symmetries and mesh-refinement consistency into a transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs without feeding coordinates directly to learned operations.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets reliable aerodynamic surrogates whose predictions remain consistent across object poses, unit changes, and boundary discretizations.
method: Uses distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, with lengths normalized by a boundary-derived scale.
Treats every boundary cell as a token and weights every boundary sum by quadrature.
Predicts interior fields through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel, with each query independent of other queries.
evidence_signal: On AeroZoo’s 2,816 flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline’s; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranks behind GLOBE but achieves at least 1.6× lower errors than Transolver and GeoTransolver.
watch_item: Results concern steady, boundary-driven PDEs; performance on unsteady turbulence and the cost of retaining every boundary cell require further evaluation.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
